questions.q: What does a successful `Database.SaveResult` from `EventBus.publish()` actually confirm?
options: That every subscriber has already received the event
That the event was queued for publishing, not that it has already been delivered to subscribers
That the triggering transaction has committed
That the event was converted into a custom object record
questions.explain: A successful SaveResult only confirms the event was queued for publishing — delivery to subscribers happens separately and isn't guaranteed by this result alone.

questions.q: If `EventBus.publish()` fails to publish an event, what happens?
options: It throws a CalloutException
It throws a DmlException
It does not throw an exception; you must check isSuccess() on the returned SaveResult and inspect getErrors()
The org automatically retries indefinitely with no way to detect the failure
questions.explain: EventBus.publish() does not throw on a failed publish — the caller must check isSuccess() and getErrors() on the Database.SaveResult explicitly.

questions.q: Which trigger event types are valid on a platform event trigger?
options: after insert, after update, after delete
before insert and after insert
after insert only
before insert, before update, and after undelete
questions.explain: A platform event is never updated or deleted after publishing — it only arrives — so a platform event trigger supports only after insert.

questions.q: In the lightning/empApi `subscribe(channelName, replayId, callback)` call, what does passing -1 as the replay ID mean?
options: Replay every event ever published on that channel
Only deliver events published from now on, not historical ones
Subscribe to all channels in the org
Unsubscribe immediately after one event
questions.explain: A replay ID of -1 tells empApi to deliver only new events published from the moment of subscription onward, which is the common choice for a live listener component.

questions.q: Why does a `@InvocableMethod` Apex action that publishes a platform event take and return a `List<Request>` / results, even for a single Flow invocation?
options: Because platform events require at least two records per publish call
Because it's a general Apex-to-Flow convention that allows the same action to run efficiently in bulk, not something unique to events
Because EventBus.publish() cannot accept a single event
Because Flow does not support scalar input variables
questions.explain: Taking and returning lists is the standard invocable-action pattern so the same method handles a bulk Flow run efficiently — it applies to any invocable Apex action, not something specific to platform events.
